site.name: pelagic
site.summary: pelagic-clone Marketing site (landing page) for the fictional open-source vector database Pelagic. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page landing: top nav + animated GitHub-stars counter pill; hero with title, dual CTAs, `pip install` copy strip, rotating benchmark numbers, right-side 4-language (Python / Node / Go / curl) code tabs; Trusted-by logo row; 3 core-feature cards; Ingest → Index → Query three-step flow; architecture SVG diagram; customer quote cards; left Blog 5 posts + right Changelog 5 entries dual feed; 4-column footer with sitemap | | `styles.css` | Brand color #0E5C8A deep-sea blue; Inter + JetBrains Mono; responsive at 3 breakpoints (>1100 / 880–1100 / <880) | | `script.js` | Stars-counter 1.2s eased animation; code tabs switch Python / Node / Go / curl; benchmark rows rotate every 2.5s; `pip install pelagic` copy toast; fictional-logo rendering |

run_plan.goal: Exercise the full single-page Pelagic landing experience, with emphasis on the hero conversion path, interactive code/benchmark controls, section navigation, and responsive/mobile usability.
run_plan.summary: The run should start in the hero and validate the primary conversion path: CTA links, install copy action, stars counter, and code tab switching. It should then move through the anchored sections to confirm the landing page structure, feature messaging, and footer navigation all behave as expected. Because this is a single HTML page, coverage should focus on distinct sections, visible controls, and mobile tap-target/regression checks rather than page-to-page traversal.
assumptions: The site is a true single-page landing site with all content in index.html and anchor-based navigation instead of separate HTML pages.
The start page already includes the full marketing content, so most validation will be section/state based rather than route based.
The visible tap-target warnings on nav items, copy button, and code tabs are relevant to verify again in mobile viewport.
The animated stars counter and rotating benchmark numbers are intended behaviors and should be checked for stability and correct state changes.
risk_hotspots: Hero CTA buttons: Quickstart and View on GitHub anchors in the primary conversion area
Install strip copy button: 'pip install pelagic' copy action and success feedback
Code language tabs: python / node / go / curl state switching in the hero code panel
Animated GitHub stars pill: live-looking counter animation and display consistency
Rotating benchmark stats: p95 latency / recall / throughput values changing on a timer
Top navigation and footer sitemap links: anchor routing across sections and possible small tap targets on mobile
Responsive layout breakpoints: stacked hero, code panel placement, and footer column wrapping below 880px

phases.title: Hero conversion and interactive controls
phases.objective: Validate the first-screen experience and the core interactive elements that drive conversion.
key_checks: Click Quickstart and confirm it scrolls/jumps to the quickstart section without breaking layout.
Click View on GitHub and confirm the link target/state is handled as expected for this clone.
Click Copy on the install command and verify a visible toast or confirmation appears.
Switch among python, node, go, and curl tabs and confirm the code sample updates cleanly for each state.
Observe the GitHub stars pill and benchmark line for animation/rotation and confirm text remains legible during updates.
exit_criteria: All hero controls have been exercised at least once.
At least one successful copy interaction is observed.
All four code tabs have been selected and their content/state changes confirmed.

phases.title: Section-by-section content scan
phases.objective: Traverse the landing page anchors and validate the major marketing sections for structure and content continuity.
key_checks: Use top nav anchors Product, Docs, Pricing, and Blog to jump to the relevant sections.
Validate the core-feature cards and the Ingest → Index → Query flow are presented in a readable sequence.
Check the architecture diagram section for rendering integrity and no overlap/clipping.
Review the customer quote cards and the blog/changelog dual feed for correct card/list formatting.
exit_criteria: Each major content region has been reached or visually confirmed.
The three-step flow and architecture section render without obvious truncation.
The blog/changelog split feed is visible and distinguishable as two columns/streams.

phases.title: Footer and sitemap link validation
phases.objective: Verify the lower-page navigation model and the sitemap-style footer links.
key_checks: Scroll to the footer and confirm the four-column sitemap is present.
Click representative footer links from each column: Overview, Hybrid search, Managed, Docs, Quickstart, Benchmarks, Migration guides, GitHub, Discord, Forum, and RFC tracker.
Confirm anchor behavior is consistent and the page does not lose state or jump to broken positions.
exit_criteria: All footer columns are reachable and visually clear.
Representative links from each footer column have been tested.
No broken anchor behavior or layout collapse is observed.

phases.title: Mobile viewport regression pass
phases.objective: Re-check the most important interactions under mobile constraints, with attention to tap target usability and layout stacking.
key_checks: Repeat the hero checks on mobile viewport: Quickstart, Copy, and one code-tab switch.
Verify the top nav compresses acceptably and remains usable or transforms safely on narrow width.
Check that the hero, code panel, and metric strip stack without horizontal overflow.
Inspect tap targets called out in the prescan as small on mobile, especially nav links, copy button, and code tabs.
exit_criteria: Core hero interactions work on mobile viewport.
No major horizontal scrolling or clipping appears.
Mobile tap-target concerns are confirmed with concrete evidence.

phases.title: Stability and edge-state review
phases.objective: Look for regressions in dynamic content, repeated interactions, and any state persistence issues.
key_checks: Re-select code tabs multiple times to ensure state changes remain stable.
Observe benchmark rotation through at least one cycle to confirm content updates do not jitter or overlap.
Return to the hero after deep scrolling and confirm anchor navigation preserves expected page state.
Check for console or layout errors after repeated interactions.
exit_criteria: Dynamic elements remain stable after repeated use.
No console errors or new layout warnings emerge during the run.
The page remains visually coherent after navigation and state toggling.

coverage_targets.pages: visit the single known HTML page (index.html) and traverse all major anchored sections
coverage_targets.features: exercise all visible hero controls, representative top-nav and footer links, code tabs, copy feedback, and at least one full benchmark animation cycle
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat the hero conversion flow, one code-tab switch, and key navigation checks in a narrow viewport, specifically checking tap-target usability

notes: Because only one HTML file is known, prioritize breadth of sections and interaction states over route discovery.
If any link resolves to a placeholder anchor, record the behavior rather than treating it as a missing page.
The known low-severity small tap-target warnings are especially important to verify on mobile, since they affect the main nav and code controls.

prescan_summary.visible_text_excerpt: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 17.8k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. The migration tool re-indexed 240M vectors without a single drop." SF Sana Falconer Staff ML Engineer, Halcyon Health From the blog 2026-05-04 Why we rewrote our HNSW build in Rust A 1,400-line memory-allocator rewrite cut index build time by 2.3× — the postmortem. Marisol Chen 2026-04-21 Pelagic 0.42: hybrid search, done right Dense + sparse + filter in a single planner. The query language, the plan, the numbers. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. PRODUCT Overview Hybrid search Managed Pricing RESOURCES Docs Quickstart Benchmarks Migration guides COMMUNITY GitHub Discord Forum RFC tracker Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Throughput: 42k QPS python node go curl import { Pelagic } from "pelagic"; const db = new Pelagic({ apiKey: "pk_live_…" }); const index = await db.createIndex({ name: "docs", dim: 1536, metric: "cosine", hybrid: true, }); await index.upsert([ { id: "doc-001", vector: await embed(text), filter: { lang: "en" } }, ]); const hits = await index.query({ vector: await embed("what is hnsw"), topK: 10, filter: { lang: "en" }, rerank: "bge-large", }); 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… p95 latency: 18ms python node go curl package main import "github.com/pelagic-io/pelagic-go" func main() { db := pelagic.New("pk_live_…") idx, _ := db.CreateIndex("docs", 1536, pelagic.Cosine, pelagic.Hybrid) idx.Upsert([]pelagic.Row{ {ID: "doc-001", Vector: embed(text), Filter: pelagic.M{"lang": "en"}}, }) hits, _ := idx.Query(pelagic.Q{ Vector: embed("what is hnsw"), TopK: 10, Filter: pelagic.M{"lang": "en"}, Rerank: "bge-large", }) _ = hits } 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Throughput: 42k QPS python node go curl package main import "github.com/pelagic-io/pelagic-go" func main() { db := pelagic.New("pk_live_…") idx, _ := db.CreateIndex("docs", 1536, pelagic.Cosine, pelagic.Hybrid) idx.Upsert([]pelagic.Row{ {ID: "doc-001", Vector: embed(text), Filter: pelagic.M{"lang": "en"}}, }) hits, _ := idx.Query(pelagic.Q{ Vector: embed("what is hnsw"), TopK: 10, Filter: pelagic.M{"lang": "en"}, Rerank: "bge-large", }) _ = hits } 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip.
